clusters.label: Agentic Evaluation and Self-Improvement
clusters.description: This cluster focuses on the development of autonomous AI agents that can interact with complex environments (robotics, visual puzzles, cybersecurity, scientific literature) and the specific frameworks or benchmarks used to evaluate their tool-use capabilities and facilitate their autonomous self-improvement through feedback loops.
dominant_methods: Agentic Tool Use and CLI Translation
clusters.rationale: All four papers center on the capabilities of LLM-based agents in specific domains. Papers 1 and 2 focus on agent architectures (harnesses/skill libraries) that enable interaction and self-improvement. Papers 3 and 4 introduce specialized benchmarks to rigorously evaluate these agents' tool-use and retrieval capabilities. The unifying theme is the transition from static models to interactive, tool-using agents and the methods to measure and enhance their performance.

clusters.label: Latent Variable Structured Generation
clusters.description: Research that builds continuous latent representations to generate complex discrete structures—such as natural language sequences or molecular graphs—while preserving global constraints through diffusion or grammar‑based decoding.
clusters.rationale: Both papers tackle the problem of generating structured discrete objects by coupling a continuous latent state with a mechanism that enforces structural validity—diffusion denoising for language and higher‑order grammar rules for molecules—hence the unified label of latent‑driven structured generation.

clusters.label: Efficient Generative Model Optimization
clusters.description: This cluster focuses on techniques to accelerate inference, reduce computational overhead, and improve the training stability of complex generative and neural models, including distillation for real-time animation, adversarial distillation for few-step image/video synthesis, topology-aware 3D generation, scalable quasi-Newton optimizers, and entropy-regularized policy optimization.
clusters.rationale: The papers share a common theme of optimizing the efficiency and performance of neural generative systems. They employ distinct but related strategies such as distillation (GALA, DMAD), efficient latent representations (SILSA), advanced optimization algorithms (SoftServe), and efficient policy learning (FERPO) to overcome computational bottlenecks in animation, image/video generation, 3D synthesis, and reinforcement learning.

clusters.label: AI Ethics and Human Agency
clusters.description: This cluster investigates the ethical, philosophical, and sociotechnical implications of AI integration, focusing on the preservation of human autonomy, the nature of trust in automated systems, and the development of policy frameworks for responsible deployment in critical and educational contexts.
clusters.rationale: All four papers address the non-technical, normative, and human-centric aspects of AI. They move beyond algorithmic performance to examine trust, user agency, ethical considerations in education, and governance in public services, collectively forming a theme of AI ethics and human-AI interaction dynamics.

clusters.label: Governance of Generative AI in East Asia
clusters.description: This cluster investigates the regulatory frameworks, ethical challenges, and policy mechanisms governing the deployment of generative AI in East Asian contexts, specifically focusing on South Korea and China. It addresses the tension between technological utility in domains like language education and media journalism, and the need for algorithmic justice, data privacy, and cultural accuracy.
clusters.rationale: Both papers focus on the intersection of generative AI and societal governance in East Asia (specifically Korea and China). One examines educational ethics and instructional governance, while the other analyzes media policy and algorithmic regulation. The shared core is the development of responsible AI frameworks and regulatory strategies in this specific geographic and cultural context.
